description: Generate a cryptographic digest or HMAC of a value, or verify a value against an expected digest. Set operation to "generate" for a digest, or "compare" to constant-time-check value against the expected digest — compare is timing-safe and avoids manual string equality checks. Omitting operation compares when expected is supplied and generates otherwise. Algorithm defaults to sha256; sha384 and sha512 are also secure, while md5 and sha1 are exposed ONLY for checksum and file-integrity compatibility and for verifying existing HMAC-SHA1 signatures, and must not be used for passwords, new signatures, or any other security purpose. Set secret to compute HMAC(algorithm, secret, value) instead of a plain digest, for generate and compare alike — the check behind webhook signatures such as GitHub's X-Hub-Signature-256 (pass the header value as expected) and HS256 JWT signatures; secretEncoding says how secret is written (utf8 default, hex, base64, or base64url for a JWK k), the result carries hmac: true, and the secret is never echoed back. digestEncoding selects the generated digest form: lowercase hex (default), base64, base64url (unpadded, the JWS signature form), or sri (<algorithm>-<base64>, the npm lockfile integrity and Subresource Integrity form, sha256/sha384/sha512 only, plain digests only). expected is recognized by its shape at the algorithm's digest length, so a published checksum can be pasted as-is: a bare hex, base64, or base64url digest; SRI, which may hold several space-separated entries as an npm integrity field can and matches when any entry for algorithm does; one checksum-file line as sha256sum, shasum, md5, or openssl dgst prints it (<hex>  <file>, or SHA256 (<file>) = <digest>); or a digest prefixed sha256: or sha256= (OCI and release-asset digests, webhook signature headers). A tag or prefix naming another algorithm fails rather than being ignored, and a multi-line checksum file must be cut to the one line for the file. inputEncoding controls how value is read before hashing (utf8 default, or hex/base64 for raw binary data) so binary blobs need no decode round-trip. The canonical use is matching a download against a vendor-published checksum or a lockfile integrity entry.

algorithm.description: Digest algorithm. sha256 (default), sha384, or sha512 for security; md5/sha1 are for checksums and for verifying existing HMAC-SHA1 signatures only — not for new security use.

digestEncoding.description: Form of the generated digest: lowercase hex (default), standard base64, base64url (URL-safe alphabet, unpadded — the JWS signature form), or sri (<algorithm>-<base64>, sha256/sha384/sha512 only, and not with secret). Applies to operation "generate".

expected.description: The digest to compare against, recognized from its shape at the algorithm's digest length: hex (any case), standard base64, or base64url, bare or prefixed as <algorithm>:<digest> or <algorithm>=<digest>; SRI (<algorithm>-<base64>); or one checksum-file line, <hex>  <file> (sha256sum, shasum, md5 -r) or SHA256 (<file>) = <digest> (BSD, --tag, openssl dgst). A string of only hex digits is always read as hex; hex split by whitespace is rejected, as is a <hex>  <file> line whose file name is only hex digits. An SRI value may carry several space-separated entries: entries for other algorithms are skipped, and it matches when any entry for algorithm matches. A tag or prefix naming another algorithm is rejected, as is a whole multi-line checksum file. Supplying it with operation omitted runs a compare; it is rejected with operation "generate".

inputEncoding.description: How value is decoded before hashing: utf8 text, hex, or base64.

operation.description: "generate" produces a digest; "compare" constant-time-checks value against expected. When omitted, resolves to "compare" if expected is supplied and "generate" otherwise.

secret.description: HMAC key. When non-empty, the digest is HMAC(algorithm, secret, value) instead of a plain hash, for generate and compare alike. Read per secretEncoding and used exactly as sent, never trimmed; an empty string counts as absent. Never echoed in the result or in error messages.

secretEncoding.description: How secret is written: utf8 text (default, as a webhook signing secret is), hex, base64, or base64url (as a JWK k member is). Read only when secret is non-empty.

value.description: The data to hash, interpreted per inputEncoding (raw text by default).

name: toolkit_hash_value

digest.description: Digest of value in the requested digestEncoding: lowercase hex, base64, unpadded base64url, or <algorithm>-<base64>; the HMAC when hmac is true. Present for operation "generate".

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `missing_expected`: operation is "compare" but no expected digest was supplied. `expected_without_compare`: operation is "generate" but an expected digest was also supplied, so it would be ignored. `expected_malformed`: expected is not a digest in any form the tool reads, spans several lines (a whole checksum file), or is an SRI value holding a token that is not an SRI entry. `expected_length_mismatch`: expected is a recognized digest form but its length does not match the algorithm, so compare would always fail. `expected_algorithm_mismatch`: expected names an algorithm other than the chosen one, in a checksum-line tag, an <algorithm>: or <algorithm>= prefix, or SRI entries none of which names the chosen algorithm. `sri_unsupported_algorithm`: digestEncoding is "sri" and algorithm is md5 or sha1, which SRI does not define. `invalid_input_encoding`: value is not valid for the declared inputEncoding (e.g. non-hex characters with inputEncoding "hex"). `invalid_secret_encoding`: secret is not valid for the declared secretEncoding (e.g. non-hex characters with secretEncoding "hex"). `sri_with_secret`: digestEncoding is "sri" on operation "generate" and a secret was supplied; SRI carries plain digests, not HMACs. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

hmac.description: Present (true) when the digest is an HMAC keyed by secret; absent for a plain digest.

lengthInBytes.description: Digest size in bytes (32 for sha256, 48 for sha384, 64 for sha512, 20 for sha1, 16 for md5). Present for "generate".

matches.description: Constant-time equality of the computed digest (the HMAC when hmac is true) against expected. Present for operation "compare".

operation.description: The operation performed, after resolving an omitted operation.

title: toolkit-mcp-server: hash value
